accepted.summary: This course explores how AI tools such as new-age IDEs, terminals, code review, and testing platforms are transforming the software development life cycle. Students combine the core principles of building complex systems with hands-on experience using state-of-the-art AI workflows through real-world tasks and team-based projects.
accepted.pedagogy_notes: Team-based project and real-world engineering tasks.
evidence_quotes: AI is rapidly transforming how we build, debug, and maintain software.
Through real-world engineering tasks and a team-based project, you'll learn not just how to use the latest AI-powered workflows, but also when and why to trust them.
accepted.relevance_reason: Matches topics on AI-assisted coding, workflows, and emerging developer tools, but lacks detailed weekly breakdown or specific agentic engineering and specification topics.

accepted.summary: This course teaches graduate students how to integrate AI tools into scientific research with rigor, treating large language models and prompting as an engineering discipline. Students cover topics including retrieval-augmented generation, AI-assisted software development, agentic systems, and evaluation frameworks, culminating in a research capstone project.
topics: evaluation frameworks for detecting and analyzing AI failures
accepted.pedagogy_notes: Students build working systems on their own research data throughout the course, culminating in a capstone project that produces a deliverable for their research group.

accepted.summary: This course introduces tools and techniques for the systematic and rigorous development of software systems, covering object-oriented analysis, modelling, design, implementation, and testing. Key topics include Unified Modelling Language (UML), program correctness, modularisation, and software quality.
evidence_quotes: This course introduces the necessary conceptual and analytical tools for systematic and rigorous development of software systems.
